title: AI editing: Remove, Select, generative fill and Replace, and sky replacement on local models
objective: Bring AI editing into Luxforge on local, user-downloaded models behind one inference port and one analysis cache: detection-driven object removal with a fill that rebuilds structure rather than blur, automatic masks that list what each photograph contains, a generative tier with variations and prompted Replace, an optional deterministic sky replacement over the Select Sky mask, and the typed remote-provider shape delivered last, every result a durable artifact rendered without the model.
context_summary: Decided by the owner on 2026-10-05 (docs/decisions.md, AI editing): the scope is accepted, models are chosen quality-first with no licence or provenance gate beyond a one-line use restriction, ONNX Runtime is the measured runtime, stale patches keep rendering, budgets are raised for quality rather than results reduced, remote consent is remembered per provider, and sky replacement is in scope. Its harness and foundation tasks are ready on the merged GPU-first renderer, with the Corrections foundation scheduled beside its first stage. The plan builds on the September 2026 object removal research, the standalone object removal prototype measured on the M4 (probes/object-removal and docs/design/object-removal.md on the claude/object-removal-research-d3374b branch, not on main), the implemented module capabilities (resources, consent, tasks, derived artifacts, two capability lanes), the implemented Settings and flags surface, and the delivered mask model and Masks panel. It takes AI Remove over from the Corrections proposal and depends by name on that proposal's foundation: the repair stage with its bounded regional primitive, the Corrections brush descriptor and draft target, and the repair layer's frozen-patch operation with prefix invalidation; those land under the Corrections plan and this plan's Remove task waits for them to be merged; until the repair stage exists the analysis input is the developed content stage, which is the repair stage's output when there are no repairs. Under GPU-first every new coverage kind and composite needs a GPU program within the declared tolerance, which the mask-kind, Remove, sky and depth tasks each require. The delivered tile service answers bounded stage rectangles through the desktop GPU tile worker or the reference renderer in luxforge-json; module tasks still need a host-planned read in ModuleContext. Owner, 2026-10-07: all AI analysis, guide, fill-crop and remote repair-crop inputs use the reference renderer. A generation locks its photograph while another photograph remains editable; progress and cancellation stay responsive. Qualification measures permitted editing during inference and combined model/renderer residency, re-checking the 24 GB generative starting minimum. Every new layer needs a CPU reference and a GPU program within the declared tolerance. No cross-file task IDs are used.

tasks.description: Record the owner's twelve AI editing decisions and freeze the recorded defaults the plan runs on.
extra_context: Completed on 2026-10-05: the owner decided every question (docs/decisions.md, AI editing); the design's Decisions table records the outcomes, the roadmap's exclusion is lifted and the Corrections design carries the stale-patch rule.

The twelve decisions and their recommendations are the Decisions table of docs/design/ai-editing.md: scope, weights licence policy, training-data provenance, the inference runtime (ONNX Runtime through ort, measured by the prototype against tract, which loads one of the five pinned models), the segmenter and Fast fill model, the generative models and runtime, the effect region, stale patches, budgets, the generative hardware minimum, sky replacement and remote consent. The prototype's move onto main as the harness is a recorded default, not a decision, so the harness task is ready now and the measurements that inform decisions 4 to 6 can start before they are taken.

Decision 8 (stale patches) differs between this design (keep rendering the frozen patch, mark it stale, ask before export) and the Corrections design (fail render, sample and export explicitly); the owner picks one and the other design is updated to match.

Decision 2 gates which models later tasks may pin: OpenRAIL++-M removers and the SAM License are offered only as explicit, off-by-default downloads if admitted; non-commercial weights are never offered. Big-LaMa's weights are labelled Apache-2.0 only by a community mirror and its Places training images carry non-commercial and no-redistribution terms, which the owner weighs against MI-GAN's MIT weights.
Budgets (decision 9) are proposals replaced by measurements; a later task completes against the recorded figure, never against an unstated one.

tasks.description: Settle the Fast fill's quality on large regions by measuring larger model inputs, a finer second pass and detail transfer, and freeze the Fast pipeline.
extra_context: The prototype's fill is enlarged 8.9x for the boy on the bridge, 10 to 13x for a flower or water, 19.7x for a tall pole and 29.8x for a 60 MP quadrant because the pinned LaMa export takes a fixed 512x512 input and the crop is three times the region's longer side; grain is re-synthesised but structure is not. The full-precision Big-LaMa export scored within 0.1 dB of the quantized one and gave the same smeared deck, so the enlargement, not the weights, is the cause.

Remedies to measure in order: a Big-LaMa export at 1024 or 2048 or with dynamic shapes (the model is fully convolutional and coherent to about 1536 px; the CPU time grows with the input area); a second LaMa pass over the region in tiles at a finer scale with the coarse fill as context; HiFill-style detail transfer that keeps the model's low and middle frequencies and rebuilds high frequencies from the surrounding context by patch matching. MI-GAN runs at 2048 natively (1.2 s on an iPad Pro M2) with MIT weights and joins the comparison.

Quality is scored with the harness on the owner corpus and the pasted-object ground truth, plus a blinded owner preference on the bridge, the sunflowers, the kayaks and the road; time and peak memory are recorded per variant at 24 and 60 MP on the M4 with the host's load noted.
Fills remain byte-identical outside the region in every variant; a variant that changes an outside pixel is rejected.

Every measured fill changed zero pixels outside its region.

tasks.description: Qualify the Select models on the M4: the semantic model, the salient-subject model, the people detector, the parts model and depth, with the class mapping and presence rules.
extra_context: Candidates from the research and the design: EoMT on a DINOv2 backbone (MIT checkpoints; the ADE20K large model at 512 has 0.3 B parameters; a COCO-Stuff checkpoint preferred for cloud and snow classes) and a 2 MB MIT U2-Net-p sky model as a Sky-only alternative; BiRefNet general and BiRefNet_HR (MIT) for Subject; RF-DETR-Seg Nano or Small (Apache-2.0) for people instances refined by a box prompt to the segmenter; MediaPipe multiclass (Apache-2.0) for hair, face skin, body skin and clothes on a person crop; Depth Anything 3 Small or Base (Apache-2.0) for depth. Each is exported to ONNX where no export exists and run through the harness on the CPU provider and Core ML.

Measured per model at the design's analysis input (at most 1024 px): latency cold and warm, peak memory, Core ML placement and fp16 parity, download size, and, for the card, whether the licence restricts the person's use of their results (the owner's quality-first policy admits every candidate and discloses no training data); the guided upsampler's cost to 4096 px is measured once.

The class mapping table and the presence rules (area share and mean confidence) in the design are starting values tuned here on the corpus: per-class IoU against hand-marked sky, water and vegetation regions on a dozen photographs, and the false-presence rate on photographs without the class.
No model is pinned until its measured figures are recorded and its licence class is confirmed.

tasks.description: Qualify the generative tier: Moebius and FLUX.2 klein 4B on the M4 within the one-toolchain rule, with the shipped prompt embedding, candidates, memory and quality against the Fast fill.
extra_context: Moebius is a 0.22 B latent inpainter that takes an image and a binary mask, about 0.9 GB per checkpoint, Apache-2.0 in its repository and MIT on its model card (confirm which before pinning); FLUX.2 klein 4B is Apache-2.0 with a 7.75 GB bf16 transformer, a 168 MB VAE and the Qwen3-4B text encoder (8 GB bf16, 3.5 GB at 4-bit), no Fill checkpoint, a RePaint-style diffusers inpainting pipeline and an Apache-2.0 removal LoRA from fal trained on 100 pairs. Published Apple-silicon figures for klein at 1024 and 4 steps: about 17 s including load at 4-bit on an M4 Max with a 6.5 GB peak, 24 to 31 s on an M1 Max; none for an M4 Pro.

Runtime candidates: stable-diffusion.cpp (MIT; Metal, Vulkan, CUDA; GGUF; supports klein with Metal, its masked path for klein undocumented) through its Rust binding or directly, built from vendored pinned sources with the cc crate as LibRaw is, with no CMake and no Python; MLX behind a C ABI only as a macOS comparison. An ONNX export of klein does not run on Core ML. If no runtime builds within the rule, the task records it and the generative tier waits for the remote tier.

Measured: cold load, warm time per candidate at 512, 768 and 1024, three candidates in a row, peak memory, download size; quality on the corpus and the ground truth against the Fast fill as the fill-quality task froze it (the prototype's 512 px fill is scored too, so an early run is not wasted), with a blinded owner preference and a reference ceiling from a non-commercial model run for evaluation only; whether a precomputed empty-scene embedding reproduces the prompted result within tolerance so the text encoder can stay out of the removal download.

OSOR-SDXL and RORem are measured beside the Apache candidates under the owner's quality-first policy of 2026-10-05, and ObjectClear and TurboClear are measured too; every candidate is ranked on quality, and a model whose terms restrict the person's use is recorded with that restriction for its card and is never a default pick.

tasks.description: Add the inference port to the core, the ONNX Runtime crate behind it, the deterministic fake, and the local-runtime capability with activation and unload.
extra_context: The port is two traits the core declares and never implements natively: Session (open a verified model file on a named backend; run named tensors in and out; report placement and precision) and Generator (image, mask, optional prompt or embedding, seed; yield candidates one at a time, cancellably). A new crate, luxforge-onnx, implements Session over ort 2.0.0-rc.13 statically linked with the Core ML provider on macOS and DirectML on Windows, writes the fixed-shape Core ML copy of a model once at install time, keeps the compile cache under the application data root keyed by model hash, runtime version and OS build, and is handed to the host through HostConfig as luxforge-net's transport is. A deterministic fake backend implementing both traits lives in luxforge-core beside the proof modules and is served only to developer runs and tests: the core-free-test-base rule keeps every workspace crate out of luxforge-testbase and the core-builds-once rule keeps the core from naming luxforge-testkit, so the fake can live nowhere else.

A dependency rule row in xtask/src/repository.rs keeps ort, ort-sys and every runtime crate out of luxforge-core's manifest, with an allowed and a refused case in its tests; add a new xtask archive check against the pinned version, SHA-256 and published attestation, with explicit failure tests; no such archive-attestation check exists today.

The local-runtime capability is defined by this consumer: a module declaring it may hold loaded sessions between tasks in a host-owned slot with a declared resident budget per model, is unloaded on a memory signal or after an idle interval (recorded default 10 minutes), is never loaded by module.list, a catalog open or a launch, and reports its resident set through module.status. The capability brings two generated methods, module.runtime.load {module_id, resource_id} (a tool's warm-up on pick) and module.runtime.unload {module_id, resource_id?} (the Models tab's Unload now), so loading and releasing are requests any client can send. CapabilityKind gains local-runtime; today serde rejects that unknown variant before registration, and managed-storage stays unsupported.
Nothing in this task renders, and no model ships: it is proven with the fake and with one pinned model file the test downloads nowhere (the harness's installed EfficientViT-SAM, opt-in).

tasks.description: Add the model-selection mask kind, artifact binding for mask components, and the shared guided upsampler with its reference.
extra_context: The kind is the masking workspace's phase E, position-based: model {artifact, class, model, model_version, input_fingerprint, prefix_hash, feather, threshold}, coverage the 8-bit alpha artifact sampled bilinearly, thresholded and feathered by the frozen smooth, bounds from the artifact's non-zero rectangle, min_feature_px from its resolution; a row of COMPONENT_KINDS in mask/mod.rs and its own file, with mask.create-model, mask.add-model and mask.set-model generated. The component-kind repository rule confines its tokens.

The kind table's Binding is {stage, strokes, mask}, with no prepared artifacts; widen it so MaskField::compile (called from modules/registry/compile.rs), preview/coverage.rs (overlays and thumbnails) and ComponentField::gpu(stage) receive resolved artifacts. Admission checks each component artifact, the prepared-artifact cache pins it for each masked layer and retention keeps it while any entry references it.

The guided upsampler is one pure-Rust function in the core (He and Sun's fast guided filter over a bounded window with a confidence-weighted prior), transcribed in f64 in luxforge-reference with bit-identity tests, used by every model mask and every removal region; the prototype's refine module is its starting point. Its guide is a luminance raster at the output's own resolution (the analysis task's cached guide at the artifact size for a selection; the source-resolution window for a removal region), never the 1024 px analysis input, so edges the reduction lost are recovered.
mask.list reports the component's model, version, computed-at time and staleness reason; Recompute and Keep are the panel's actions over the task and mask.set-model.

The model kind ships GpuProgramKind::Coverage (render/gpu/program.rs). GpuDescription carries uniform words and an optional Arc<[u32]> storage block, not an artifact texture binding; the host concatenates blocks into one buffer bounded by max_storage_buffer_binding_size. Implement bounded bilinear alpha reads through that block contract, or extend the core description and both GPU hosts with an artifact-binding contract; do not assume an existing texture slot. Prove sampling, threshold and feather against CPU coverage, including adapter binding limits. mask.add-model and mask.set-model refuse by name when the stack exceeds the 256 MiB prepared-artifact budget.

The delivered release gate, cargo xtask gpu-qualification, runs in verify --tier rendered. CPU coverage remains exact against its f64 reference. Charge each artifact upload and binding allocation on each device: to the 2 GiB GPU-preview budget on the photo surface and separately to the tile worker's 2 GiB GPU_TILE_BUDGET; warm-up covers the new program. A missing coverage program yields no-program and reference rendering for the affected stack, including its picture, reads and export.

Add model-mask recipe rows to fixtures/preview/corpus.json: each has id, family, class, description, source IDs and evidence-script steps. A small checked-in alpha fixture and deterministic fake task reproduce the bound artifact through those steps; extend fixture setup only where needed. Qualification covers the picture at every view, counts, reads and export; the gate judges only recipes the corpus carries.

tasks.description: Implement the analysis tasks and cache, the hover worker and the picker query, and the object selection task on the luxforge.ai module.
extra_context: Three tasks run on the module lane, one per installed model set, because a task's declared resources must all be installed before it may run: task.analyse {asset_id} runs the segmenter's encoder (Remove and Objects); task.analyse-scene {asset_id} runs the semantic model, the salient-subject model (Subject, and Background as its inverse) and the people detector (Select); task.analyse-depth {asset_id} runs the depth model. Each renders the analysis input (the repair stage's output reduced to at most 1024 px, the developed content stage until the Corrections repair stage exists, which is the same thing when there are no repairs) and the one-channel luminance guide at the artifact resolution (at most 4096 px, at most 16 MiB), and fills a bounded in-memory cache (recorded default 256 MiB, least recently used) keyed by source fingerprint, repair-prefix hash (the host's repair-stage boundary using spatial::prefix_hash over its upstream layers and masks with the actual sampling mode) and model identity and version. Each result lists what it found (classes with area share and confidence, the subject, people with bounds, model versions); an unchanged input answers from the cache, and the cache's bytes count in the machine-memory minimum beside the resident models.

The hover worker is one thread of its own, started with the first Remove or Objects pick and stopped with it, holding the loaded decoder and the current embedding and keeping only the latest pointer position; its output is view state. It joins the declared worker homes in the thread-spawn repository rule.

query.pick-object {asset_id, prompt} is the picker's programmatic form: a point, points with labels, a box or a stroke become prompts as the prototype's stroke module does, candidates are scored on predicted IoU, stability, stroke coverage and object coverage, parts yield to wholes, duplicates are suppressed largest first, and the decision is One, Several or Nothing with fixed tie order. task.select-object publishes the chosen candidate as an alpha artifact through the guided upsampler against the cached guide.

The desktop's hover overlay is sampled from the candidate's logits over its bounds, under a pixel cap, so the frame uploads within its budget; the hover's pointer-to-overlay latency is measured in a hidden window as the prototype measured it.

The analysis cache's budget adds a memory target, so it is a named constant in the architecture's limits table and an owner-accepted budget (decisions, 2026-09-30: a cache whose budget adds to a memory target needs the owner's acceptance), not a private default.

Every AI pixel read uses a host-planned bounded stage read. ModuleContext has no pixel-read port today: add one that holds an immutable evaluation and cancellation off the owner, using the reference reads in luxforge_core::tiles, independently of the host's production GPU provider. TileSession::read reads ReadStage::Before {layer, mode} rectangles in ReadValues::Linear, bounded to one evaluated frame per read; TileService::stream provides output-stage RGBA8 bands for export, not arbitrary-prefix bands. Reduce tiled reads on the module lane, with the host selecting the stage boundary and sampling mode. TILE_QUEUE_CAPACITY is nine (eight clients plus desktop); define bounded admission for module reads without silently enlarging it. Owner, 2026-10-07: every AI input uses reference reads on every host. Source, repair-prefix, model, runtime and precision remain explicit identities; identical reference inputs do not promise identical inference across execution providers.

Owner, 2026-10-07: qualify the permitted editing and UI responsiveness during inference, and model machine minima against combined resident models, candidates, cache and renderer resources. Remove is a takeover canvas mode of the Corrections module (mode strip, proposed letter Q), with hover highlight, click, Alt-click, box and stroke through the picker; the selection is the object core, the stroke footprint and an effect region (the contact-band suggestion, off until the person turns Detect shadow on, refined with Add and Subtract); Several shows numbered pins with Confirm and Cancel; Nothing removes the painted footprint.

task.fill-fast {asset_id, selection, effect_region?} runs the frozen Fast pipeline on the module lane against a held revision and prefix (the generative and remote tiers are separate tasks of the same request and result shape, so an optional model is never a prerequisite of Fast); its result is candidates addressed by job and index, at most 4 of at most 64 MiB per job and 1 GiB across jobs, the oldest finished job's released first and reported on job.read, never dropped because another job completed or the tool was left; the Corrections accept action rechecks revision and prefix, publishes the chosen patch as an artifact and commits one operation labelled Remove, storing the selection, transforms, prefix hash and provenance. Admission: a region of at most 32 MP and half the frame; the crop is bounded only by the frame and reduced to the model's input size, with the enlargement notice past the recorded threshold. Accept checks that the stack's artifacts bind within the 256 MiB prepared-artifact budget and refuses by name past it. The repair composite's GPU program is the Corrections foundation's; this task proves the committed patch renders within the declared tolerance on the GPU on the corpus, display, samples and export alike.

The held-candidate budget is likewise a named constant in the limits table and an owner-accepted budget; the committed patch is held to the reference by cargo xtask gpu-qualification for the picture, samples and export through the delivered GPU tile worker.

tasks.description: Implement the remote provider module with the repair-crop data class, one hosted adapter and the documented loopback service protocol.
extra_context: The remote module publishes the same candidates and patches as the local provider through task.fill-remote {asset_id, selection, effect_region?, profile_id, candidates?, prompt?}, which declares the remote-image-request capability, so the recipe cannot tell them apart. Its adapter declares the repair-crop data class (an sRGB 8-bit crop of at most 2048 px on the long side with its coverage mask, the prompt, the candidate count; no path, EXIF or full frame), bearer authentication with the key in the OS credential store, request and response limits, timeout, retention note and cost; a full-frame class, if a provider needs it, is a separate class with its own consent.

Consent is remembered per provider profile and data class until revoked (owner, 2026-10-05), which changes the capability contract's remote-image-request grant scope to drop the asset; the disclosure states the bytes, the destination and the retention note, nothing is sent before the first Generate and its grant, and Revoke all withdraws it. The capability design and user guide change with it. Responses are validated for dimensions, format, finite values and size; a refusal, timeout, disconnect or malformed answer leaves the recipe untouched.

The first hosted provider is the owner's choice; the loopback protocol is documented so a person can run their own service, and luxforge-testbase gains a fake provider on the loopback test server for every malformed, error and cancel case with exact sent-byte inspection. extra_context: Measured on the M4 Pro on a quiet host with the pinned models and photo-sized inputs: hover pointer-to-overlay, analysis-ready time after the tool is picked, warm model loads, a class selection's time, the Fast fill at 24 and 60 MP, a generative candidate and three in a row, peak resident memory per model and for the whole resident set, download sizes, and the idle cost of the hover worker and the analysis cache; each against the recorded budget, with misses published beside the scope.

Quality: the harness scores on the owner corpus and the CC0 corpus for the Fast and generative fills, the per-class IoU for Select, and the blinded preference test the owner runs against Lightroom's Remove and Generative Remove on the same photographs and masks.

The optional slices (sky, parts and depth, the remote provider) add their own evidence to the same package when they land; this task does not wait for them. A local generative no-go is recorded as such and the generative figures are omitted with the reason, never inferred.
Timing runs wait until the feature work above is merged and take the host-wide timing lock; the full tier states every skipped component.

Owner, 2026-10-07: qualify the permitted editing and UI responsiveness during inference, and model machine minima against combined resident models, candidates, cache and renderer resources. Report the two separate 2 GiB renderer budgets as ceilings, not allocations; measure residency and omitted GPU overhead separately, and re-check the 24 GB generative starting minimum. Run timing once feature work is complete.

Owner, 2026-10-07: a new generation locks only its photograph, through the command service as well as the desktop; another photograph remains editable and progress and cancellation stay responsive. Accepted patches render without inference. Qualification exercises permitted editing on another photograph while inference runs; it does not require same-photograph slider edits during generation.
